prompt: The query in the editor has one mistake. Fix it so that it answers this question: which campaigns spent more than the average campaign of their channel? Count all the spend in ad_spend_daily, and average over the campaigns of the channel that have spend. Compare with the exact average. Return four columns, in this order: campaign_id, channel_id, spend (the campaign's total spend) and channel_avg, the channel's average campaign spend rounded to 2 decimals. Return one row for each such campaign. Any row order is fine.
hints: Next, move the comparison out of the query that works out the window: name the channel average in a step first.
WHERE picks rows before any window is worked out, so the average must be a named column of a WITH step before the outer WHERE can test it.
starter_sql:
WITH campaign_spend AS (  -- one row per campaign with spend
  SELECT c.campaign_id, c.channel_id, SUM(a.spend) AS spend
  FROM ad_spend_daily a
  JOIN campaigns c ON c.campaign_id = a.campaign_id
  GROUP BY c.campaign_id, c.channel_id
)
SELECT campaign_id, channel_id, spend, ROUND(AVG(spend) OVER (PARTITION BY channel_id), 2) AS channel_avg
FROM campaign_spend
WHERE spend > AVG(spend) OVER (PARTITION BY channel_id)
why_this_works: The window is worked out in a WITH step and named, so the outer WHERE can test it: WHERE never sees a window in its own query.
